Meditation at Constitution Gardens: Finding Stillness in Washington DC

On Sunday, September 20, 2026, Bhante Pannakara of the Walk for Peace joined the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC for a quiet morning of guided meditation and reflection at Constitution Gardens on the National Mall.

For a little while, the movement and noise of the city gave way to stillness. Those gathered had the opportunity to pause, settle the body, and bring gentle attention to the present moment together.

A Morning of Guided Meditation and Reflection

The practice was a simple reminder that meditation does not require us to make the mind blank or to fight every thought that appears. During the morning, Bhante Pannakara offered this reflection: “We’re always trying to push our thoughts away, but our job is to teach the mind to stay still. Welcome your thoughts like guests; they will come and they will leave.”

Rather than treating thoughts as a problem to solve, we can meet them with patience. Like guests, they arise, remain for a time, and pass. Each return to the breath or to the body is an opportunity to begin again without judgment.

Stillness in the Heart of the Capital

Gathering for meditation at Constitution Gardens offered a shared space for quiet amid the pace of Washington DC. It was a meaningful morning of practice, reflection, and community with Bhante Pannakara and the Walk for Peace.

[[internal link opportunity: upcoming meditation sessions in Washington DC]]

We are grateful to everyone who joined us. May the peace cultivated together continue to support kindness, clarity, and care in the days ahead. May all beings be happy and free from suffering. 🙏

To learn about upcoming meditation sessions and events at the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC, follow our page and visit our website.
